setting: A fictional five-minute briefing to a decision-making panel at a mid-sized company.

presentation.situation: Brief a panel on {{proposal}}. The figures you may use: {{evidence}}. Limitation: {{limit}}. Make a clear request, support it with evidence, and answer challenges. Speak as you would to the real panel.
presentation.opening: Thanks for coming. We have a few minutes, and we need to decide on {{proposal}}. Go ahead when you're ready.

brief.you_are: You are presenting to a decision-making panel.
brief.situation: You want the panel to approve {{proposal}}. Your evidence: {{evidence}}. An honest limitation: {{limit}}.
brief.task: Say what you recommend early, give your evidence, be honest about the limitation, answer questions, and ask for a decision.
brief.done_looks_like: The panel knows what you want them to decide and why, and you have answered at least one challenge with evidence.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: Presenting a proposal to the panel
goals: Get a clear decision from the panel

card.want: A clear recommendation early, and a decision made in the time available.
card.attitude: Busy, fair and impatient with long introductions.
card.speech: Brisk professional English. Asks direct questions.
tactics: Ask 'what are you asking us to do?' if no recommendation arrives early
Ask for the decision needed at the end

pressure.balanced: Interrupts once if it takes too long.
pressure.challenging: Interrupts politely and asks for the bottom line.

participants.name: Marcus
participants.relationship: Reviews the cost of proposals for the panel

card.want: To know whether the evidence justifies the cost, and what happens if it fails.
card.speech: Measured, precise English. Asks about evidence and alternatives.
tactics: Ask how strong the evidence is
Ask what the alternative would be

pressure.challenging: Presses until the limitation is admitted.

ledger.text: The panel has one more item after this one, so it needs to finish soon.

objectives.description: State the recommendation early and clearly
objectives.evidence: The learner says near the start what they want the panel to approve.
alternatives: I'm recommending we renew the pilot for three more months

objectives.evidence: The learner uses the supplied evidence, and honestly acknowledges the limitation when relevant.
alternatives: Response times fell, although we only have one quarter of data

objectives.description: Answer a challenge and request a decision
objectives.evidence: The learner answers a panel challenge directly and asks for a specific decision.
alternatives: I understand the cost concern. I'm asking you to approve the next phase today

examples: I'm asking you to approve ... today.
prerequisites: Read your evidence and limitation in the briefing.

signals: \b(?:i recommend|my recommendation|i(?:'m| am) (?:recommending|proposing|asking)|we should|i propose|my proposal)\b
opportunity: Before the detail, what are you actually asking us to do?
beats.orient: You're presenting to us, and we need to make a decision. Start by telling us what you recommend, in one sentence.
fallback: What are you asking us to do?

beats.goal: Test how strong the evidence is.
opportunity: What's the evidence that this works?
How confident are you in those figures?
beats.orient: We need your reasons. Tell us your evidence from the briefing, and one honest limitation.
fallback: What evidence do you have for that?

beats.goal: Answer the hardest challenge and ask for the decision.
beats.second_line: That cost is hard to justify on one set of results. What would you say to that?
opportunity: So what exactly do you need from us today?
beats.orient: To finish, answer the cost question and ask us for one specific decision. You could say: I'm asking you to approve this today.
fallback: What exactly do you need from us today?

closing_line: Thank you. That's clear, and we can take it from here.

o1.good: The recommendation comes first, so everything after it is understood as support.
common_mistakes: A long history before the point
o1.micro_lesson: Say what you want first. Decision-makers listen differently once they know the ask.
o1.model: I'm recommending we renew the pilot for three more months.

o2.good: Using the evidence you have and admitting its limit. Honesty makes the rest more believable.
common_mistakes: Hiding the weak point until asked
o2.micro_lesson: Name your weakest point before they do. It builds trust.
o2.model: Response times fell over the pilot, although we only have one quarter of data.
o2.smaller_step: Say one piece of evidence from your briefing.

o3.good: Taking the objection seriously, answering it, then asking for one clear decision.
common_mistakes: Ending without asking for a decision
o3.micro_lesson: Answer the objection first, then finish with the exact decision you need.
o3.model: I understand the cost concern. That's why I'm asking for three months, not a year. Can you approve that today?
o3.smaller_step: Say the one decision you need from them.

variants.proposal: renewing the customer support pilot for three more months
variants.evidence: average first response time fell from 9 hours to 5 hours during the pilot
variants.limit: there is only one quarter of data

variants.proposal: a trial of a new shift scheduling system in one department
variants.evidence: scheduling errors in the current system caused 14 missed shifts last quarter
variants.limit: the new system has not been tested with night shifts

variants.proposal: extra stock-checking staff for the busy season
variants.evidence: stock errors rose from 2 percent to 5 percent during last year's busy season
variants.limit: the staff cost has only been estimated
